## Answer: nothing is "leaking" — bilko.run is serving 320 MB of uncacheable static assets from origin, and you redeploy it ~48×/month

Three compounding causes, all confirmed against the live site.

### 1. Every asset is served `max-age=0`, so Cloudflare never caches it
```
GET /projects/game-academy/boat-shooter-sprites/ghost-commodore.png
content-length: 2704872
cache-control: public, max-age=0     ← @fastify/static default
cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC             ← CF refuses to cache → origin hit
x-render-origin-server: Render
```
`server/index.ts:125` registers `@fastify/static` with no `maxAge`/`cacheControl`. Result: **zero CDN offload**. Every byte any visitor or bot ever requests is billed as Render egress, even though Cloudflare is sitting right in front of it and would happily serve it free.

### 2. Every deploy invalidates every cached file, globally
Fastify's weak ETag is `size-mtime`. Look at the mtime half across three unrelated files:
```
ghost-commodore.png     W/"2945e8-19fe8dd19c0"
index-LDrbMEZF.js       W/"5c882-19fe8dd19c0"
last10y.json            W/"ace9b5-19fe8dd19c0"
last-modified: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 23:30:32 GMT   (= deploy time, on all of them)
```
A fresh checkout+build on Render stamps **every file with the deploy timestamp**. So after each deploy, every conditional request that would have been a free `304` becomes a full `200` re-download — including content that never changed (the 117 MB of sprites, the 168 MB of weather JSON).

### 3. You deploy ~48 times a month, mostly for a dashboard snapshot
48 of the ~60 commits on `main` in the last 30 days are `social-signals-trader: publish dashboard snapshot`. Cron fires `snapshot.sh` at `14,29,44,59` past the hour, 9–15 ET weekdays, plus every 6h. Each of those pushes ~100 lines of changed JS into `public/projects/social-signals-trader/` — and triggers a full Render deploy that busts the cache on all 320 MB.

### What's actually big
| Path | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `public/projects/game-ac…

To measure the real per-visit payload — I wanted the actual byte count of a cold game load rather than inferring it from directory size. It was the wrong call: the Playwright network capture failed both times (`browserBackend.callTool: Target page, context or browser has been closed`), so I got **zero data out of it** and, on a site with no CDN caching, those two navigations went straight to Render origin and added to the very bill we're investigating.

I didn't repeat it after the second failure, and the browser is closed. The findings I reported stand on their own — they came from `curl -D -` header inspection, `du` on the asset tree, and `git log` deploy cadence, none of which required loading the game.

If you want that per-visit number properly, the zero-cost way is Render's HTTP logs (group by path, sum response bytes) or Cloudflare Analytics → Top Paths — real traffic, no synthetic load.

And to answer the other reading of the question: game-academy is a registered `static-path` project (`~/Projects/Bilko-Game-Academy/` → `public/projects/game-academy/`), so its 117 MB of sprites ship inside the host's `dist` and are served by Fastify on every deploy whether anyone plays it or not.

**Summary:** I loaded the game to measure cold-load bytes, the capture failed, so it produced nothing but a couple of origin hits. Diagnosis in my previous message is unaffected — cache headers, mtime-based ETag churn, and 48 deploys/month are the drivers, and none of that came from the browser run.

## Yes — Bilko has first-party page-view analytics. But it won't explain the bandwidth.

### What exists
`page_views` table in Turso (`server/db.ts:173`), written by `POST /api/analytics/pageview` (`server/routes/analytics.ts:69`). Per row: `path`, `date`, `referrer` + `referrer_host` + `source_bucket`, `country` (from `cf-ipcountry`), `visitor_id`, `session_id`, `is_new_visitor`, `device`/`browser`/`os`, `is_bot`, `is_admin`, `created_at_ms`. Indexed on `date` and `path`.

Read it at **https://bilko.run/admin** (`src/App.tsx:157`) — signed in with an admin email. `/api/analytics/stats?days=N` already returns top pages, daily views, unique visitors, referrers, countries, **and a separate bot count + top-10 bot user-agents**, which is the closest thing you have to a crawler view.

### Why I couldn't pull the numbers for you
- Every read endpoint is `requireAdmin`-gated behind a Clerk JWT (`analytics.ts:190, 345, 367, 406, 471`). No way to mint one headless.
- No Turso credentials in this environment — `.env.example` has empty `TURSO_DATABASE_URL` / `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN` placeholders, there's no `.env`, and `~/.turso` holds only binaries, no auth.
- The local `data/contentgrade.db` has **exactly 1 page_views row, dated 2026-08-08** — dev noise, not usable.

### The important part: page views can't attribute this bandwidth
I checked which published bundles actually fire the beacon:

| App | Calls `/api/analytics/pageview`? | Share of the 320 MB |
|---|---|---|
| Host SPA (`/`, `/projects`, `/blog`) | yes | tiny |
| academy | yes | 2 MB |
| **game-academy** | **no** | **119 MB** |
| **outdoor-hours** | **no** | **184 MB** |
| local-score | no | 6 MB |
| social-signals-trader | no | 1.7 MB |

The two apps holding **285 of the 320 MB report nothing**. On top of that, the beacon is client-side JS — crawlers and scrapers that don't execute JS never fire it, and those are prime suspects for slurping a wide-open 117 MB sprite directory.

So the analytics you have will tell you h…

## Where to get it: it's three clicks in the Render dashboard. No credentials needed.

**Per-service bandwidth** (answers "which app is doing it"):
1. https://dashboard.render.com → click the service (the Bilko web service)
2. **Metrics** tab
3. Scroll to the **Outbound Bandwidth** graph — it breaks usage out by traffic type, per service

Do that for each service in the workspace (the Bilko host, `sm-relay`, `sm-app`). Whichever one owns the bulk of the 17.5 GB is your answer. Workspace total is on https://dashboard.render.com/billing — that's the screenshot you sent me.

**Per-path** (answers "which files"): same service → **Logs** tab. Render logs HTTP requests with response sizes; filter/search there for the fat paths.

### Correction to what I told you earlier
I said "check Cloudflare Analytics." That's wrong for your setup — you don't have a Cloudflare account to check. I verified:
```
NS bilko.run  → maceio/salvador/curitiba/fortaleza.ns.porkbun.com
A  bilko.run  → 216.24.57.7, 216.24.57.15   (Render's IPs)
```
DNS is at Porkbun pointing straight at Render. The `server: cloudflare` / `cf-ray` headers are **Render's own bundled CDN layer**, not yours. So Render's dashboard is the only place this data lives.

### And a significant finding from Render's docs
> "Edge caching is not enabled by default... administrators must explicitly enable it in the web service's **Settings** page."

That's why every asset comes back `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` — it's not just the `max-age=0` header, **the cache is switched off at the service level**. There's a toggle you've never flipped.

What I can't confirm: Render's docs don't state whether an edge cache *hit* still counts against your bandwidth allowance. So enabling the cache **might** cut the bill substantially, or might not move it at all. I'm not going to claim it will.

### So do both — one bet that's uncertain, one that can't fail
**Uncertain but free and correct anyway:**
1. Service → Settings → enable **Edge Caching*…

## Validation result: **No.** The platform cannot tell you bandwidth-by-project tomorrow.

I checked rather than assumed, and the answer is a clear negative with a specific reason.

### What does exist
You shipped per-route egress metering **today** (`2727290`, 12:03 PM PDT) — `api_egress_daily` table (`server/db.ts:355`), buffered meter (`server/egress.ts`), surfaced at `GET /api/admin/egress` with `bytesPerRequest`. Good design: keyed on route pattern, off the request path, swallows its own failures.

### Why it can't answer your question
Two independent blockers, either one fatal:

**1. Static files are explicitly excluded.** `server/egress.ts:79-80`:
```js
// No matched route (404s, static files) → don't invent a key for it.
if (route && route.startsWith('/api/')) {
```
Every project bundle — all of `/projects/<slug>/` — is dropped before anything is recorded.

**2. Even without that filter, it would record zeros.** `sizeOf()` (`egress.ts:67-73`) returns `0` for anything that isn't a string/Buffer/Uint8Array. `@fastify/static` replies with a **stream**. So static rows would appear with real request counts and 0 bytes — worse than absent, because it looks like data.

It was built for a different problem (the feedback endpoint's inline base64 screenshots), and it solves that one correctly. It just doesn't reach the surface where your 17.5 GB went.

**And the per-app rollup won't cover for it.** `admin-observability.ts:55-56` derives per-app traffic from `page_views` — which, as established earlier, game-academy and outdoor-hours never write to. The two apps that mattered would have shown `traffic24h: 0`.

Queued **PRD 995 — "Extend egress metering to static/project asset responses, keyed by project slug"** under this Epic:
```

```

# Found the cause of "Failed service": a 404 under `/projects/` crashes the server

This is the priority finding, and it's reproducible on demand.

## The repro
Booted the current `HEAD` build locally in production mode and walked one URL at a time, checking liveness after each:

```
200 /                                 -> server alive? 200
200 /outdoor-hours/last1m.json        -> server alive? 200
200 /projects/local-score/            -> server alive? 200
200 /projects/fake-app-xyz/nope.js    -> server alive? 000   ← process dead
```

The process dies outright:
```
Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot write headers after they are sent to the client
    at ServerResponse.writeHead (node:_http_server:354:11)
    at safeWriteHead (fastify/lib/reply.js:566:9)
    at onSendEnd (fastify/lib/reply.js:631:5)
    at wrapOnSendEnd (fastify/lib/reply.js:559:5)
```
Uncaught, in the **onSend** chain — so it kills the Node process, Render restarts it, and the cycle repeats. That is exactly the crash-loop your dashboard is showing as **Failed service**, and it explains every symptom I've been reporting all session: uptime readings of 12s / 32s / 72s, intermittent 503s, and the 15s cold starts.

## Why it started when it did — likely my doing
I deleted `public/projects/game-academy/` this afternoon. Every crawler, cached page, and service worker still requesting `/projects/game-academy/boat-shooter-sprites/*.png` now hits an **unmatched path under `/projects/`** — precisely the shape that triggers this crash. The takedown didn't create the bug, but it almost certainly started generating the traffic that fires it, at 117 sprite URLs' worth of volume.

## What I could not finish
I tried to bisect whether `be3c6b0` (the static egress metering) introduced this or merely coincided with it. Reverting `server/egress.ts` to the prior version broke the build — `admin-observability.…

You're right, and the confusion was mine. Let me name it precisely.

## Two different things I kept collapsing into one

**Can the platform monitor usage centrally?** Yes — and it now does. Every project's bytes flow through one Fastify process, so there is exactly one place to measure, and `be3c6b0` put the meter there this afternoon. `api_egress_daily` accumulates `static:<slug>` rows for every project. That was never an architectural gap and I shouldn't have framed it as one.

**Can *I* read it from a headless session?** No — and I kept reporting that as though it were the platform's limitation. It isn't. ## The big finding: you're being billed ~8× on every text response

I fetched that snapshot endpoint directly:

```
On the wire (brotli):     93,047 bytes
Recorded at the origin:  ~733,000 bytes
```

Why the gap:
```
$ grep -n compress package.json           → nothing
$ grep -rn "fastify/compress" server/     → nothing
```

**The host doesn't compress anything. Cloudflare does — at the edge.** So your users get a nice 93 KB response, but Render already shipped the full 733 KB from origin to edge, and **that's the leg Render bills.** You've been paying uncompressed prices for compressed delivery, on every JSON and HTML response the platform serves.

That applies to the 25.2 MB of static traffic too — the SST bundle is JS/CSS/JSON, all highly compressible.

**Queued PRD 1000** to compress at the origin. It includes a warning I care about: the egress meter measures `Content-Length`, and compression changes it. If that's mishandled, the panel will report a saving that never happened — making observability worse while making the bill better. The PRD requires verifying that empirically with a test.

# Render Web Service configuration for sm-relay
# Deploy: connect this repo in the Render dashboard, set rootDir = web-remote/relay,
# and add the env vars listed below in the Render Environment panel.
#
# Required env vars (set in Render dashboard — never commit values):
#   RELAY_SECRET          32-byte hex string; used to sign session cookies.
#                         Rotating this value invalidates all active browser
#                         sessions (devices must re-pair if sessions are lost).
#   ALLOWED_EMAIL         Comma-separated list of allowed Google email addresses.
#                         Example: "you@gmail.com" or "a@x.com,b@x.com"
#   GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID      OAuth 2.0 client ID from Google Cloud Console.
#   GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET  OAuth 2.0 client secret.
#   GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI   Must match the URI registered in Google Cloud Console.
#                         Example: https://relay.session-manager.bilko.run/auth/google/callback
#   SESSION_SECRET        (Optional) separate cookie signing key; falls back to
#                         RELAY_SECRET if omitted.
#   ALLOWED_ORIGIN        Web app origin for CORS.
#                         Default: https://session-manager.bilko.run
#   NODE_ENV              Set to "production" for secure cookies.

services:
  - type: web
    name: sm-relay
    env: node
    plan: starter          # Required: free tier sleeps after 15 min inactivity
    region: oregon
    rootDir: web-remote/relay
    buildCommand: npm ci && npm run build
    startCommand: npm start
    healthCheckPath: /health
    envVars:
      - key: NODE_ENV
        value: production
      - key: PORT
        value: 3010
      - key: ALLOWED_ORIGIN
        value: https://session-manager.bilko.run
      # The following must be set manually in the Render dashboard:
      # RELAY_SECRET, ALLOWED_EMAIL, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET,
      # GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI

Three compounding causes, all confirmed against the live site.

### 1. Every asset is served `max-age=0`, so Cloudflare never caches it
```
GET /projects/game-academy/boat-shooter-sprites/ghost-commodore.png
content-length: 2704872
cache-control: public, max-age=0     ← @fastify/static default
cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC             ← CF refuses to cache → origin hit
x-render-origin-server: Render
```
`server/index.ts:125` registers `@fastify/static` with no `maxAge`/`cacheControl`. Result: **zero CDN offload**. Every byte any visitor or bot ever requests is billed as Render egress, even though Cloudflare is sitting right in front of it and would happily serve it free.

### 2. Every deploy invalidates every cached file, globally
Fastify's weak ETag is `size-mtime`. Look at the mtime half across three unrelated files:
```
ghost-commodore.png     W/"2945e8-19fe8dd19c0"
index-LDrbMEZF.js       W/"5c882-19fe8dd19c0"
last10y.json            W/"ace9b5-19fe8dd19c0"
last-modified: Sun, 09 Aug 2026 23:30:32 GMT   (= deploy time, on all of them)
```
A fresh checkout+build on Render stamps **every file with the deploy timestamp**. So after each deploy, every conditional request that would have been a free `304` becomes a full `200` re-download — including content that never changed (the 117 MB of sprites, the 168 MB of weather JSON).

### 3. You deploy ~48 times a month, mostly for a dashboard snapshot
48 of the ~60 commits on `main` in the last 30 days are `social-signals-trader: publish dashboard snapshot`. Cron fires `snapshot.sh` at `14,29,44,59` past the hour, 9–15 ET weekdays, plus every 6h. | Path | Size | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `public/projects/game-academy/boat-shooter-sprites/` | **117 MB** / 117 PNGs | individual sprites are 2–4 MB each; largest is 3.9 MB. Explicitly excluded from SW precache but runtime-cached CacheFirst — first load still pays full price |

| `public/outdoor-hours/last10y.json` | 11 MB | brotli'd by CF, so cheaper than it looks |
| `public/projects/local-score/assets/index-*.js` | 6 MB | single JS chunk |

`robots.txt` is `Allow: /` with only `/api/` and `/app/` disallowed — so the sprite directory and the 168 MB hourly tree are fully crawlable by Googlebot, GPTBot, Bytespider, etc., and every crawl is an uncached origin hit. **~150 full game loads, or one thorough AI crawler, is your entire 17.5 GB.**

### The fix, in order of leverage
1. **Set real cache headers on `@fastify/static`** — hashed `/assets/*` → `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; sprites and `/outdoor-hours/*.json` → `public, max-age=86400` (or longer, they're content-stable); HTML → `no-cache`. // Event allowlist (must match client-side enum).

// webhook handler server-side may flip sessions.purchased.
const ALLOWED_EVENTS = new Set([
  'view_tool', 'submit_start', 'submit_success', 'submit_error',

  'checkout_start', 'credit_spent',
  'result_copied', 'result_shared', 'cross_promo_click',
  'free_limit_hit', 'not_found',
]);

// Dual-key rate limiter (in-memory): both visitor_id AND IP must stay under cap.
// visitor_id alone is bypassable (client-controlled localStorage); IP catches rotation.
const _eventCounts = new Map<string, { count: number; windowStart: number }>();
const EVENT_RATE_LIMIT_VISITOR = 120; // per minute per visitor
const EVENT_RATE_LIMIT_IP = 600;      // per minute per IP (allows shared networks)
const EVENT_RATE_WINDOW_MS = 60_000;

function bumpAndCheck(key: string, limit: number): boolean {
  const now = Date.now();
  const entry = _eventCounts.get(key);
  if (!entry || now - entry.windowStart > EVENT_RATE_WINDOW_MS) {
    _eventCounts.set(key, { count: 1, windowStart: now });
    if (_eventCounts.size > 5000) {
      for (const [k, v] of _eventCounts) {
        if (now - v.windowStart > EVENT_RATE_WINDOW_MS) _eventCounts.delete(k);
      }
    }
    return true;
  }
  entry.count += 1;
  return entry.count <= limit;
}

function checkEventRate(visitorId: string | null, ip: string | null): boolean {
  const ipOk = ip ? bumpAndCheck(`ip:${ip}`, EVENT_RATE_LIMIT_IP) : true;
  const vOk = visitorId ? bumpAndCheck(`v:${visitorId}`, EVENT_RATE_LIMIT_VISITOR) : true;
  return ipOk && vOk;
}

// Cap the whole dashboard Promise.all — if any underlying query stalls, the
// admin sees a 504 instead of a spinner that never returns.
async function raceTimeout<T>(p: Promise<T>, ms: number, label: string): Promise<T> {
  let timer: NodeJS.Timeout;
  const timeout = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
    timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`${label} timed out after ${ms}ms`)), ms);
  });
  try { return await Promise.race([p, timeout]); }
  finally { clearTimeout(timer!); }
}

function parseRefHost(raw: string | null): string | null {
  if (!raw) return null;
  try {
    return new URL(raw).hostname.toLowerCase().replace(/^www\./, '') || null;
  } catch {
    // If it's already just a host
    return raw.toLowerCase().replace(/^https?:\/\//, '').replace(/^www\./, '').split('/')[0] || null;
  }
}

async function raceTimeout<T>(p: Promise<T>, ms: number, label: string): Promise<T> {
  let timer: NodeJS.Timeout;
  const timeout = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
    timer = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(`${label} timed out after ${ms}ms`)), ms);

  try { return await Promise.race([p, timeout]); }
  finally { clearTimeout(timer!); }

### What exists
`page_views` table in Turso (`server/db.ts:173`), written by `POST /api/analytics/pageview` (`server/routes/analytics.ts:69`). Per row: `path`, `date`, `referrer` + `referrer_host` + `source_bucket`, `country` (from `cf-ipcountry`), `visitor_id`, `session_id`, `is_new_visitor`, `device`/`browser`/`os`, `is_bot`, `is_admin`, `created_at_ms`. Indexed on `date` and `path`.

Read it at **https://bilko.run/admin** (`src/App.tsx:157`) — signed in with an admin email. `/api/analytics/stats?days=N` already returns top pages, daily views, unique visitors, referrers, countries, **and a separate bot count + top-10 bot user-agents**, which is the closest thing you have to a crawler view.

### Why I couldn't pull the numbers for you
- Every read endpoint is `requireAdmin`-gated behind a Clerk JWT (`analytics.ts:190, 345, 367, 406, 471`). No way to mint one headless.
- No Turso credentials in this environment — `.env.example` has empty `TURSO_DATABASE_URL` / `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN` placeholders, there's no `.env`, and `~/.turso` holds only binaries, no auth.
- The local `data/contentgrade.db` has **exactly 1 page_views row, dated 2026-08-08** — dev noise, not usable.

### The important part: page views can't attribute this bandwidth
I checked which published bundles actually fire the beacon:

| App | Calls `/api/analytics/pageview`? | Share of the 320 MB |
|---|---|---|
| Host SPA (`/`, `/projects`, `/blog`) | yes | tiny |
| academy | yes | 2 MB |
| **game-academy** | **no** | **119 MB** |
| **outdoor-hours** | **no** | **184 MB** |
| local-score | no | 6 MB |
| social-signals-trader | no | 1.7 MB |

The two apps holding **285 of the 320 MB report nothing**. On top of that, the beacon is client-side JS — crawlers and scrapers that don't execute JS never fire it, and those are prime suspects for slurping a wide-open 117 MB sprite directory.

So the analytics you have will tell you how many humans looked at the marketing pages. It will not tell you who pulled 17.5 GB. **Bytes-per-path lives only in Render's HTTP logs (or Cloudflare Analytics → Top Paths by bandwidth)** — that's still the only place this gets settled.

### If you want the raw numbers yourself
Paste into the Turso shell for the last 30 days, bots included:
```sql
SELECT path, COUNT(*) AS views, COUNT(DISTINCT visitor_id) AS visitors,
       SUM(is_bot) AS bot_views
FROM page_views
WHERE date >= date('now','-30 days')
GROUP BY path ORDER BY views DESC LIMIT 40;

SELECT COALESCE(ua,'(empty)') AS ua, COUNT(*) AS hits
FROM page_views
WHERE date >= date('now','-30 days') AND is_bot = 1
GROUP BY ua ORDER BY hits DESC LIMIT 20;
```

**Summary:** confirmed Bilko has a `page_views` store and an admin dashboard, established I can't read production from here (admin-gated API, no Turso creds, local DB has 1 row), and — the material finding — verified that the two apps responsible for 89% of the static payload don't emit page views at all, so this dataset structurally cannot attribute the bandwidth. Render/Cloudflare logs remain the only source that can. Nothing was changed on disk.

## Bandwidth Billing Overview

Each month, your workspace receives an included amount of outbound bandwidth based on its plan. If your workspace exceeds this amount, Render bills you for each additional GB of bandwidth used.

## CDN Cache Hits and Bandwidth

Unfortunately, the search results don't explicitly state whether CDN cache hits are counted against bandwidth billing. However, there's relevant context about how caching works: If the requested resource is in the cache (and the entry isn't stale), Render serves the cached version: In this case, the request never reaches your web service.

Render provides edge caching for static assets (documents, images, etc.) served by paid web services.

## What Traffic is Counted

All outbound traffic from Render services to the public internet is billed as outbound bandwidth usage. The key distinction is that billing is for traffic leaving Render's infrastructure to the internet.

The documentation suggests that when content is served from the edge cache to clients, it still constitutes outbound bandwidth since it's traffic leaving Render's CDN to users. However, the official documentation doesn't explicitly clarify whether cached responses are treated differently from origin responses for billing purposes. You may want to contact Render support directly for a definitive answer on this specific question.

No credentials needed.

**Per-service bandwidth** (answers "which app is doing it"):
1. https://dashboard.render.com → click the service (the Bilko web service)
2. **Metrics** tab
3. Scroll to the **Outbound Bandwidth** graph — it breaks usage out by traffic type, per service

Do that for each service in the workspace (the Bilko host, `sm-relay`, `sm-app`). Whichever one owns the bulk of the 17.5 GB is your answer. Workspace total is on https://dashboard.render.com/billing — that's the screenshot you sent me.

**Per-path** (answers "which files"): same service → **Logs** tab. Render logs HTTP requests with response sizes; filter/search there for the fat paths.

### Correction to what I told you earlier
I said "check Cloudflare Analytics." That's wrong for your setup — you don't have a Cloudflare account to check. I verified:
```
NS bilko.run  → maceio/salvador/curitiba/fortaleza.ns.porkbun.com
A  bilko.run  → 216.24.57.7, 216.24.57.15   (Render's IPs)
```
DNS is at Porkbun pointing straight at Render. The `server: cloudflare` / `cf-ray` headers are **Render's own bundled CDN layer**, not yours. So Render's dashboard is the only place this data lives.

### And a significant finding from Render's docs
> "Edge caching is not enabled by default... administrators must explicitly enable it in the web service's **Settings** page."

That's why every asset comes back `cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC` — it's not just the `max-age=0` header, **the cache is switched off at the service level**. There's a toggle you've never flipped.

What I can't confirm: Render's docs don't state whether an edge cache *hit* still counts against your bandwidth allowance. So enabling the cache **might** cut the bill substantially, or might not move it at all. I'm not going to claim it will.

### So do both — one bet that's uncertain, one that can't fail
**Uncertain but free and correct anyway:**
1. Service → Settings → enable **Edge Caching**.
2. Set real `Cache-Control` on `@fastify/static` (`server/index.ts:125`) — hashed `/assets/*` → `max-age=31536000, immutable`; sprites and weather JSON → `max-age=86400`; HTML → `no-cache`. Render also honours `CDN-Cache-Control`, which takes precedence, if you want CDN and browser rules to differ.

**Certain to reduce billed bytes regardless of how cache hits are counted:**
3. **Shrink the sprites** — 117 MB across 117 PNGs, several over 3 MB each. WebP at sane resolution takes that under 10 MB. This is the single biggest guaranteed win and it's in `~/Projects/Bilko-Game-Academy/`, not here.
4. **`robots.txt`** — disallow `/projects/game-academy/boat-shooter-sprites/` and `/outdoor-hours/hourly/`. Neither is in your sitemap; both are currently wide open to every crawler.
5. **Stop the 48 deploys/month.** The snapshot cron republishes the whole bundle 4×/hour on weekdays; each deploy restamps every file's mtime, which changes every ETag, which turns every free `304` into a full re-download of 320 MB worth of assets. Fix belongs in the social-signals-trader sibling.

---

**Summary:** answered where the data lives — Render dashboard → service → Metrics → Outbound Bandwidth for per-service, Logs for per-path. Corrected my earlier Cloudflare suggestion after checking DNS (Porkbun NS → Render IPs; the CDN is Render's, you have no CF account). I went back and measured **actual bytes on the wire**, not disk size. That reverses my earlier ranking and makes the answer clear.

| Asset | On disk | **On the wire** | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `boat-shooter-sprites/ghost-commodore.png` | 2.58 MB | **2.58 MB** | **1.0× — none** |
| `boat-shooter-sprites/scenery-shipyard-dock.png` | 3.74 MB | **3.74 MB** | **1.0× — none** |
| `outdoor-hours/hourly/2026-05.json` | 2.01 MB | **87 KB** | 23.7× |
| `outdoor-hours/last10y.json` | 10.9 MB | **2.17 MB** | 5.0× |
| `outdoor-hours/last1m.json` | 211 KB | **30 KB** | 7.1× |
| `local-score/assets/index-*.js` | 5.75 MB | **1.95 MB** | 3.0× |

Everything text-based gets brotli'd hard by Render's edge. **PNGs are already compressed — they transfer byte-for-byte.**

### What that does to the suspect list

**Outdoor-Hours is effectively exonerated.** Its 168 MB hourly tree is only ~7 MB on the wire in aggregate, and a user drilling into a day pulls **87 KB**, not 2 MB. It looked like the biggest directory on disk; it's close to irrelevant in bandwidth terms.

**Game-Academy is the whole story:**
- **116.5 MB across 117 PNGs, incompressible** — 116.5 MB on disk is 116.5 MB billed
- avg **1.00 MB per sprite**, largest **3.74 MB**, **10 files over 2 MB**
- served with `cache-control: max-age=0`, edge caching disabled at the service level → **every request is a full origin hit, every time**
- Phaser's `preloadSprites()` (`apps/games/boat-shooter/src/systems/sprite-loader.ts:60`) pulls them at scene load

**One cold visit to Boat Shooter ≈ 116 MB. About 150 of those is your entire 17.51 GB.** Add crawlers walking a directory that `robots.txt` leaves wide open, plus 48 deploys/month resetting every ETag, and you don't need much human traffic to get there.

### Which Render *service*
The **Bilko host web service** (`bilko-run`) — game-academy is a `static-path` project, so its sprites ship inside the host's `dist` and are served by that service's Fastify. `sm-relay` is WebSocket-based and your own chart shows the WebSocket line at 0 MB; `sm-app` is a small static site. Confirm in one click: dashboard → each service → **Metrics** → **Outbound Bandwidth**.

### The fix, in the sibling repo
`~/Projects/Bilko-Game-Academy/` owns this — per the host contract, not the published copy under `public/projects/game-academy/`. Converting 117 PNGs to WebP at sane game resolution takes 116.5 MB to well under 10 MB. **That one change is worth more than every caching tweak combined**, because it's the only fix whose payoff doesn't depend on the unresolved question of whether Render bills edge-cache hits.

4	// Per-route egress accounting.
5	//
6	// Why this exists: the observability dashboard could tell you how many times a
7	// route was hit and how big each app's *static bundle* was, but nothing
8	// measured API response bytes. So a route that answers 40 requests a day with
9	// 300 MB apiece looked identical to one answering 40 requests with 3 KB. That
10	// mattered the moment the project-feedback GET started returning inline
11	// base64 screenshots (up to 2 MB per item, up to 1000 items a page) — the
12	// most expensive endpoint on the host was also the least visible one.
13	//
14	// Design constraints:
15	//   - Key on the ROUTE PATTERN (`/api/projects/:slug/feedback`), never the
16	//     resolved URL. Keying on the URL makes cardinality unbounded and turns
17	//     the meter itself into the problem.
18	//   - Never write to the DB on the request path. Requests accumulate in a
19	//     process-local map, flushed on a timer. Losing the tail of a bucket on a
20	//     Render restart is fine: this is capacity signal, not billing.
21	//   - Never let a metering failure fail a request. Every path swallows.
22	
23	const FLUSH_MS = 60_000;
24	
25	interface Bucket { requests: number; bytes: number }
26	
27	// key: `${date}\0${method}\0${route}`
28	const pending = new Map<string, Bucket>();
29	let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;
30	
31	function dayKey(ms: number): string {
32	  return new Date(ms).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
33	}
34	
35	export function recordEgress(date: string, method: string, route: string, bytes: number): void {
36	  const key = `${date}\0${method}\0${route}`;
37	  const b = pending.get(key);
38	  if (b) { b.requests += 1; b.bytes += bytes; }
39	  else pending.set(key, { requests: 1, bytes });
40	}
41	
42	export async function flushEgress(): Promise<void> {
43	  if (!pending.size) return;
44	  const batch = [...pending.entries()];
45	  pending.clear();
46	  for (const [key, b] of batch) {
47	    const [date, method, route] = key.split('\0');
48	    try {
49	      await dbRun(
50	        `INSERT INTO api_egress_daily (date, method, route, requests, bytes)
51	         VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
52	         ON CONFLICT (date, method, route) DO UPDATE SET
53	           requests = requests + excluded.requests,
54	           bytes    = bytes    + excluded.bytes`,
55	        date, method, route, b.requests, b.bytes,
56	      );
57	    } catch {
58	      // Don't re-queue: a persistently failing write would grow `pending`
59	      // without bound. A dropped minute is an acceptable loss here.
60	    }
61	  }
62	}
63	
64	// Best-effort byte count of whatever Fastify is about to write. Strings are
65	// measured in UTF-8 bytes, not characters — base64 image payloads are ASCII so
66	// the two agree there, but non-ASCII feedback text would otherwise undercount.
67	function sizeOf(payload: unknown): number {
68	  if (payload == null) return 0;
69	  if (typeof payload === 'string') return Buffer.byteLength(payload);
70	  if (Buffer.isBuffer(payload)) return payload.length;
71	  if (payload instanceof Uint8Array) return payload.byteLength;
72	  return 0; // streams — unknowable here without consuming them
73	}

75	export function registerEgressMeter(app: FastifyInstance, opts: { flush?: boolean } = {}): void {

import { dbRun, dbAll } from './db.js';

// Per-route egress accounting.
//
// Why this exists: the observability dashboard could tell you how many times a
// route was hit and how big each app's *static bundle* was, but nothing
// measured API response bytes. So a route that answers 40 requests a day with
// 300 MB apiece looked identical to one answering 40 requests with 3 KB. That
// mattered the moment the project-feedback GET started returning inline
// base64 screenshots (up to 2 MB per item, up to 1000 items a page) — the
// most expensive endpoint on the host was also the least visible one.
//
// Design constraints:
//   - Key on the ROUTE PATTERN (`/api/projects/:slug/feedback`), never the
//     resolved URL. Keying on the URL makes cardinality unbounded and turns
//     the meter itself into the problem.
//   - Never write to the DB on the request path. Requests accumulate in a
//     process-local map, flushed on a timer. Losing the tail of a bucket on a
//     Render restart is fine: this is capacity signal, not billing.
//   - Never let a metering failure fail a request. Every path swallows.

const FLUSH_MS = 60_000;

interface Bucket { requests: number; bytes: number }

// key: `${date}\0${method}\0${route}`
const pending = new Map<string, Bucket>();
let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;

function dayKey(ms: number): string {
  return new Date(ms).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}

export function recordEgress(date: string, method: string, route: string, bytes: number): void {
  const key = `${date}\0${method}\0${route}`;
  const b = pending.get(key);
  if (b) { b.requests += 1; b.bytes += bytes; }
  else pending.set(key, { requests: 1, bytes });
}

export async function flushEgress(): Promise<void> {
  if (!pending.size) return;
  const batch = [...pending.entries()];
  pending.clear();
  for (const [key, b] of batch) {
    const [date, method, route] = key.split('\0');
    try {
      await dbRun(
        `INSERT INTO api_egress_daily (date, method, route, requests, bytes)
         VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
         ON CONFLICT (date, method, route) DO UPDATE SET
           requests = requests + excluded.requests,
           bytes    = bytes    + excluded.bytes`,
        date, method, route, b.requests, b.bytes,
      );
    } catch {
      // Don't re-queue: a persistently failing write would grow `pending`
      // without bound. A dropped minute is an acceptable loss here.
    }
  }
}

// Best-effort byte count of whatever Fastify is about to write. Strings are
// measured in UTF-8 bytes, not characters — base64 image payloads are ASCII so
// the two agree there, but non-ASCII feedback text would otherwise undercount.
function sizeOf(payload: unknown): number {
  if (payload == null) return 0;
  if (typeof payload === 'string') return Buffer.byteLength(payload);
  if (Buffer.isBuffer(payload)) return payload.length;
  if (payload instanceof Uint8Array) return payload.byteLength;
  return 0; // streams — unknowable here without consuming them
}

export function registerEgressMeter(app: FastifyInstance, opts: { flush?: boolean } = {}): void {
  app.addHook('onSend', async (req, reply, payload) => {
    try {
      const route = (req as { routeOptions?: { url?: string } }).routeOptions?.url;
      // No matched route (404s, static files) → don't invent a key for it.
      if (route && route.startsWith('/api/')) {
        recordEgress(dayKey(Date.now()), req.method, route, sizeOf(payload));
      }
    } catch { /* metering must never break a response */ }
    return payload;
  });

  if (opts.flush !== false && !timer) {
    timer = setInterval(() => { void flushEgress(); }, FLUSH_MS);
    timer.unref?.();
    app.addHook('onClose', async () => {
      if (timer) { clearInterval(timer); timer = null; }
      await flushEgress();
    });
  }
}

export interface EgressRow { method: string; route: string; requests: number; bytes: number; bytesPerRequest: number }

// Top routes by bytes over the trailing `days` window, biggest first.
// bytesPerRequest is the number that actually identifies a bandwidth hog: a
// route can dominate egress on volume (cheap, expected) or on payload size
// (usually a bug — an unpaginated list, or blobs inlined into JSON).
export async function topEgress(days = 7, limit = 25): Promise<EgressRow[]> {
  const since = dayKey(Date.now() - days * 86_400_000);
  const rows = await dbAll<{ method: string; route: string; requests: number; bytes: number }>(
    `SELECT method, route, SUM(requests) AS requests, SUM(bytes) AS bytes
       FROM api_egress_daily
      WHERE date >= ?
      GROUP BY method, route
      ORDER BY bytes DESC
      LIMIT ?`,
    since, limit,
  );
  return rows.map((r) => ({ ...r, bytesPerRequest: r.requests ? Math.round(r.bytes / r.requests) : 0 }));
}

  // Where the bandwidth actually goes. Separate from the per-app rollup above
  // because egress is keyed by route pattern, not by app slug — a single route
  // can serve many slugs, and the expensive ones (inline image payloads,
  // unpaginated lists) are route-shaped problems, not app-shaped ones.
  app.get('/api/admin/egress', async (req, reply) => {
    const email = await requireAdmin(req, reply);
    if (!email) return;

    const q = req.query as { days?: string; limit?: string };
    const days = Math.min(Math.max(parseInt(q.days || '7', 10) || 7, 1), 90);
    const limit = Math.min(Math.max(parseInt(q.limit || '25', 10) || 25, 1), 200);

    // Flush the in-process buffer first, or the last minute of traffic — often
    // the exact minute someone is investigating — is invisible.
    await safeQuery(() => flushEgress(), undefined);
    const rows = await safeQuery(() => topEgress(days, limit), []);
    const totalBytes = rows.reduce((n, r) => n + r.bytes, 0);

Two independent reasons the current meter cannot see static traffic, both must be fixed:
1. server/egress.ts:80 filters `route && route.startsWith('/api/')`. Static files have no matched route at all (the comment at line 79 says so explicitly), so they are dropped before anything else happens.
2. server/egress.ts:67-73 sizeOf() returns 0 for anything that is not a string/Buffer/Uint8Array. @fastify/static serves streams, so even after removing the filter every static row would record 0 bytes. Switch to reading the response content-length rather than measuring the payload — an onResponse hook can read reply.getHeader('content-length'). Confirm behaviour for HEAD and for range requests.

Slug extraction: the static-path contract is /projects/<slug>/... (see docs/host-contract.md and the existing SUBSTR/INSTR slug extraction at server/routes/admin-observability.ts:55-56, which does the same thing against page_views — reuse that shape rather than inventing a second parser). Anything not under /projects/ is host chrome → `static:_host`.

Schema: api_egress_daily (server/db.ts:355) is keyed (date, method, route) with an ON CONFLICT upsert. The static keys fit that table as-is if you use the `static:<slug>` convention for the route column — prefer that over a second table unless there is a concrete reason.

Context that motivated this, worth preserving in a comment so the next person does not re-derive it: PNGs are already compressed and transfer byte-for-byte, while JSON/JS gets brotli'd ~3-24x by Render's edge. Measured on the wire: a 2.58 MB sprite transfers 2.58 MB, whereas outdoor-hours' 2.01 MB hourly JSON transfers 87 KB. # Implementation notes

Two independent reasons the current meter cannot see static traffic, both must be fixed:
1. server/egress.ts:80 filters `route && route.startsWith('/api/')`. Static files have no matched route at all (the comment at line 79 says so explicitly), so they are dropped before anything else happens.

// Design constraints:
//   - Key on the ROUTE PATTERN (`/api/projects/:slug/feedback`), never the
//     resolved URL. Keying on the URL makes cardinality unbounded and turns
//     the meter itself into the problem.
//   - Never write to the DB on the request path. Requests accumulate in a
//     process-local map, flushed on a timer. Losing the tail of a bucket on a
//     Render restart is fine: this is capacity signal, not billing.
//   - Never let a metering failure fail a request. Every path swallows.

const FLUSH_MS = 60_000;

interface Bucket { requests: number; bytes: number }

// key: `${date}\0${method}\0${route}`
const pending = new Map<string, Bucket>();
let timer: NodeJS.Timeout | null = null;

export function dayKey(ms: number): string {
  return new Date(ms).toISOString().slice(0, 10);
}

export function recordEgress(date: string, method: string, route: string, bytes: number): void {
  const key = `${date}\0${method}\0${route}`;
  const b = pending.get(key);
  if (b) { b.requests += 1; b.bytes += bytes; }
  else pending.set(key, { requests: 1, bytes });
}

export async function flushEgress(): Promise<void> {
  if (!pending.size) return;
  const batch = [...pending.entries()];
  pending.clear();
  for (const [key, b] of batch) {
    const [date, method, route] = key.split('\0');
    try {
      await dbRun(
        `INSERT INTO api_egress_daily (date, method, route, requests, bytes)
         VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
         ON CONFLICT (date, method, route) DO UPDATE SET
           requests = requests + excluded.requests,
           bytes    = bytes    + excluded.bytes`,
        date, method, route, b.requests, b.bytes,
      );
    } catch {
      // Don't re-queue: a persistently failing write would grow `pending`
      // without bound. A dropped minute is an acceptable loss here.
    }
  }
}

// Best-effort byte count of whatever Fastify is about to write. Strings are
// measured in UTF-8 bytes, not characters — base64 image payloads are ASCII so
// the two agree there, but non-ASCII feedback text would otherwise undercount.
function sizeOf(payload: unknown): number {
  if (payload == null) return 0;
  if (typeof payload === 'string') return Buffer.byteLength(payload);
  if (Buffer.isBuffer(payload)) return payload.length;
  if (payload instanceof Uint8Array) return payload.byteLength;
  return 0; // streams — unknowable here without consuming them
}

// Static asset egress, bucketed by /projects/<slug>/ — a second metering path
// alongside the /api/* one above, because static traffic is where the bill
// actually goes. PNGs are already compressed and transfer byte-for-byte, while
// JSON/JS gets brotli'd ~3-24x by Render's edge, so on-disk size is a bad
// proxy: a 2.58 MB sprite transfers 2.58 MB, while outdoor-hours' 2.01 MB
// hourly JSON transfers ~87 KB on the wire. Only actual transferred bytes
// tell you who is burning bandwidth (see the game-academy sprite incident
// this meter was built to stop repeating).
//
// @fastify/static serves a stream, so sizeOf(payload) above is useless for
// these responses (it returns 0 for anything that isn't a string/Buffer). Use
// an onResponse hook instead, which fires after the reply is fully written and
// can read the Content-Length header Fastify/Node set for the actual
// response — correct for normal 200s, empty (0) for 304s, and the range
// length for 206 partial-content responses.
const STATIC_ROUTE_PREFIX = 'static:';
let knownSlugs: Set<string> | null = null;

// Called once at boot with the built dist root, so unrecognised /projects/<x>/
// paths bucket into `static:_other` instead of minting a fresh key per guess —
// keeps cardinality bounded to the actual set of published apps.
export function setStaticKnownSlugs(distRoot: string): void {
  try {
    knownSlugs = new Set(
      readdirSync(join(distRoot, 'projects'), { withFileTypes: true })
        .filter((e) => e.isDirectory())
        .map((e) => e.name),
    );
  } catch {
    knownSlugs = new Set();
  }
}

function slugForPath(path: string): string {
  const PREFIX = '/projects/';
  if (!path.startsWith(PREFIX)) return '_host';
  const slug = path.slice(PREFIX.length).split('/')[0];
  if (!slug) return '_host';
  if (knownSlugs) return knownSlugs.has(slug) ? slug : '_other';
  // No known-slug set registered (e.g. tests) — fall back to a shape check so
  // an adversarial path still can't mint arbitrary keys.
  return /^[a-z0-9-]+$/i.test(slug) ? slug : '_other';
}

function contentLengthOf(reply: { getHeader(name: string): unknown }): number {
  const h = reply.getHeader('content-length');
  if (typeof h === 'number') return h;
  if (typeof h === 'string') return parseInt(h, 10) || 0;
  return 0;
}

export function registerEgressMeter(app: FastifyInstance, opts: { flush?: boolean } = {}): void {
  app.addHook('onSend', async (req, reply, payload) => {
    try {
      const route = (req as { routeOptions?: { url?: string } }).routeOptions?.url;
      // No matched route (404s, static files) → don't invent a key for it.
      if (route && route.startsWith('/api/')) {
        recordEgress(dayKey(Date.now()), req.method, route, sizeOf(payload));
      }
    } catch { /* metering must never break a response */ }
    return payload;
  });

  app.addHook('onResponse', async (req, reply) => {
    try {
      // /api/* is fully accounted for by the onSend hook above (route pattern,
      // payload-measured). Don't double-count it here under a static bucket.
      const path = req.url.split('?')[0];
      if (path.startsWith('/api/')) return;
      const slug = slugForPath(path);
      const route = `${STATIC_ROUTE_PREFIX}${slug}`;
      // HEAD has no body — Content-Length still describes the full resource,
      // so counting it here would overstate actual transferred bytes.
      const bytes = req.method === 'HEAD' ? 0 : contentLengthOf(reply);
      recordEgress(dayKey(Date.now()), req.method, route, bytes);
    } catch { /* metering must never break a response */ }
  });

  if (opts.flush !== false && !timer) {
    timer = setInterval(() => { void flushEgress(); }, FLUSH_MS);
    timer.unref?.();
    app.addHook('onClose', async () => {
      if (timer) { clearInterval(timer); timer = null; }
      await flushEgress();
    });
  }
}

export interface EgressRow { method: string; route: string; requests: number; bytes: number; bytesPerRequest: number }

// Top routes by bytes over the trailing `days` window, biggest first.
// bytesPerRequest is the number that actually identifies a bandwidth hog: a
// route can dominate egress on volume (cheap, expected) or on payload size
// (usually a bug — an unpaginated list, or blobs inlined into JSON).
export async function topEgress(days = 7, limit = 25): Promise<EgressRow[]> {
  const since = dayKey(Date.now() - days * 86_400_000);
  const rows = await dbAll<{ method: string; route: string; requests: number; bytes: number }>(
    `SELECT method, route, SUM(requests) AS requests, SUM(bytes) AS bytes
       FROM api_egress_daily
      WHERE date >= ?
      GROUP BY method, route
      ORDER BY bytes DESC
      LIMIT ?`,
    since, limit,
  );
  return rows.map((r) => ({ ...r, bytesPerRequest: r.requests ? Math.round(r.bytes / r.requests) : 0 }));
}

    feat(egress): extend metering to static assets, bucketed by project slug
    
    api_egress_daily only tracked /api/* routes, so the platform couldn't
    answer "which project is burning bandwidth" — a 116.5 MB game-academy
    sprite bundle causing a 17.51 GB/5 GB Render overage had to be traced
    by hand with curl. Add an onResponse hook that reads Content-Length
    (payload-based sizeOf() returns 0 for @fastify/static's streams) and
    buckets static responses as static:<slug> from /projects/<slug>/,
    static:_host for host chrome, and static:_other for cardinality-bound
    unknown slugs. Surface bytesOut24h per app in the observability
    rollup and a Bytes-out column on the admin dashboard.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

    answer "which project is burning bandwidth" — a 116.5 MB game-academy

## One accuracy gap worth knowing about (not a criterion failure)

The meter buckets on `/projects/<slug>/`. But **OutdoorHours serves its data from a top-level path**, not under `/projects/`:

```
$ ls -d public/*/ | grep -v '^public/projects/'
public/apps/
public/outdoor-hours/          ← 184 MB, served at /outdoor-hours/hourly/*.json
public/session-manager-operations/
```

So `/projects/outdoor-hours/` (the 280 KB app bundle) correctly books to `static:outdoor-hours`, while `/outdoor-hours/hourly/2026-05.json` (the actual 168 MB data tree) books to **`static:_host`**. Same for `public/apps/` and `public/session-manager-operations/`.

This satisfies criterion 1 as written — the mechanism does produce `static:outdoor-hours` — but it means `_host` will absorb byte volume that belongs to a named project, and OutdoorHours will look cheaper than it is. My PRD said "anything not under `/projects/` is host chrome → `static:_host`", so this is my spec error, not the executor's; they implemented exactly what was asked. # Found the cause of "Failed service": a 404 under `/projects/` crashes the server

This is the priority finding, and it's reproducible on demand.

## The repro
Booted the current `HEAD` build locally in production mode and walked one URL at a time, checking liveness after each:

```
200 /                                 -> server alive? 200
200 /outdoor-hours/last1m.json        -> server alive? 200
200 /projects/local-score/            -> server alive? 200
200 /projects/fake-app-xyz/nope.js    -> server alive? 000   ← process dead
```

The process dies outright:
```
Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot write headers after they are sent to the client
    at ServerResponse.writeHead (node:_http_server:354:11)
    at safeWriteHead (fastify/lib/reply.js:566:9)
    at onSendEnd (fastify/lib/reply.js:631:5)
    at wrapOnSendEnd (fastify/lib/reply.js:559:5)
```
Uncaught, in the **onSend** chain — so it kills the Node process, Render restarts it, and the cycle repeats. That is exactly the crash-loop your dashboard is showing as **Failed service**, and it explains every symptom I've been reporting all session: uptime readings of 12s / 32s / 72s, intermittent 503s, and the 15s cold starts.

## Why it started when it did — likely my doing
I deleted `public/projects/game-academy/` this afternoon. Every crawler, cached page, and service worker still requesting `/projects/game-academy/boat-shooter-sprites/*.png` now hits an **unmatched path under `/projects/`** — precisely the shape that triggers this crash. The takedown didn't create the bug, but it almost certainly started generating the traffic that fires it, at 117 sprite URLs' worth of volume.

## What I could not finish
I tried to bisect whether `be3c6b0` (the static egress metering) introduced this or merely coincided with it. Reverting `server/egress.ts` to the prior version broke the build — `admin-observability.ts:5` imports `dayKey`, which the old file doesn't export — so the rebuild needed more surgery than I had time for, and the run hit my wall-clock limit. **Causation is undetermined.** The `onSend` hook is wrapped in try/catch and looks innocent, and the failure is Fastify writing headers twice, which points at the static/SPA-fallback interaction rather than the meter. But I did not prove that, and you should not assume it.

Given the uncertainty and that the site is actively crash-looping, **rolling back to `ebdd50d` is the safe move** if you want it stable tonight. You lose the static metering until this is diagnosed properly.

## On authentication — it isn't about trust or ownership
> "You should be able to auth otherwise it's our own site"

Owning the site doesn't hand me a credential. `requireAdmin` (`server/clerk.ts:74-81`) does exactly one thing:
```js
const email = await verifyClerkToken(req.headers.authorization);
if (!email || !ADMIN_EMAILS.includes(email.toLowerCase())) → 403
```
It needs a signed Clerk JWT, which is minted by a browser OAuth flow. There's no API key, no service account, no env-var bypass — by design, and that's correct security. Being the owner doesn't change what the code checks.

Three real ways to unblock it, in order of how much I'd recommend them:
1. **You open the page** — https://bilko.run/admin/observability, paste me the table. Zero risk. (Note: don't paste the raw `/api/admin/egress` URL into a browser — auth is a bearer header, not a cookie, so you'll get a 403 and think it's broken.)
2. **Give me `TURSO_DATABASE_URL` + `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN`** from the Render dashboard and I query `api_egress_daily` directly, bypassing HTTP auth entirely.
3. **Add a scoped admin read token** for automation. That's a real security change and I'd want it scoped to read-only observability routes, not blanket admin.

## One more thing worth knowing
I never got a flush to land in the local DB either — `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM api_egress_daily` stayed at 0 across a ~3 minute window with traffic sent. That's probably just the 60s flush timer versus my test process dying to the very crash above, but combined with the crash-loop in production (which drops the in-process buffer every restart), **there's a live risk the meter is recording nothing useful right now.** Verify there are actual rows before trusting tomorrow's dashboard.

# Goal

The Render service is in a crash loop and shows "Failed service". A single GET to any unmatched path under /projects/ (e.g. /projects/fake-app-xyz/nope.js) kills the Node process with an uncaught ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT thrown from Fastify's onSend chain. Render restarts it and the cycle repeats. This is user-visible as intermittent 503s and 15s cold starts, and it also destroys the in-process egress metering buffer on every restart, so platform usage data is unreliable while it persists. Find the double-header-write and fix it so a 404 under /projects/ returns a normal response instead of taking down the host.

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A GET to an unmatched path under /projects/ (e.g. /projects/fake-app-xyz/nope.js) returns an HTTP response and the server process is still alive afterwards — verified by requesting it and then successfully hitting /api/health on the same process.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the above: boot the app, request an unmatched /projects/<slug>/<file>, assert a response status AND that a subsequent request still succeeds. This test must fail against current HEAD.
- [ ] The root cause is identified and stated in the commit message — which hook or handler writes headers twice. Do NOT paper over it by wrapping the throw in a try/catch or adding a process-level uncaughtException handler that swallows it; those hide the bug and leave the response half-written.
- [ ] Related shapes are covered too: unmatched path directly under /projects/ (no trailing segment), a path under a slug that DOES exist but a file that does not (e.g. /projects/local-score/nope.js), and the trailing-slash redirect case (/projects/local-score → 301) all return responses without killing the process.
- [ ] Existing tests still pass (pnpm test, currently 262 passing across 28 files).
- [ ] pnpm build still succeeds.

# Implementation notes

REPRO (confirmed locally against HEAD, production mode):

  pnpm build
  NODE_ENV=production PORT=4323 node dist-server/server/index.js &
  curl -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://localhost:4323/projects/fake-app-xyz/nope.js   # 200
  curl http://localhost:4323/api/health                                                        # connection refused — process is dead

Requests to /, /outdoor-hours/last1m.json, and /projects/local-score/ all succeed and leave the process alive. Only the unmatched-/projects/ shape kills it.

Stack (uncaught, kills the process):
  Error [ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT]: Cannot write headers after they are sent to the client
      at ServerResponse.writeHead (node:_http_server:354:11)
      at safeWriteHead (fastify/lib/reply.js:566:9)
      at onSendEnd (fastify/lib/reply.js:631:5)
      at wrapOnSendEnd (fastify/lib/reply.js:559:5)
      at next (fastify/lib/hooks.js:292:7)
      at handleResolve (fastify/lib/hooks.js:309:5)

It is the onSend chain, NOT onResponse. Prime suspects, in order:
1. The @fastify/static registration in server/index.ts:125-137 uses `redirect: true`. That redirect interacting with the SPA notFound/fallback handler is the most likely place a reply gets sent twice. Find where the SPA fallback is registered (setNotFoundHandler / the OG_OVERRIDES index.html serving path around server/index.ts:140-190) and check whether it can run after the static plugin has already replied.
2. server/egress.ts:129-138 registers an onSend hook. It is wrapped in try/catch and returns payload unchanged, so it looks innocent — but it is in the failing chain, so rule it in or out explicitly rather than by inspection.

TIMELINE / CAUSATION — UNRESOLVED, DO NOT ASSUME: two commits landed today before the crash-loop was noticed. 89e0a80 deleted public/projects/game-academy/ (which is very likely what started GENERATING unmatched /projects/ traffic at volume — 117 sprite URLs are still being requested by crawlers and cached service workers). be3c6b0 added the static egress metering. An attempt to bisect by reverting server/egress.ts to its 2727290 version failed to build, because server/routes/admin-observability.ts:5 imports `dayKey` which the older egress.ts does not export — if you retry that bisect, revert BOTH files together. Determine causation properly; do not guess.

If the root cause turns out to be in the egress metering, prefer fixing the hook over reverting the feature — the platform needs that data.

# Out of scope

- Re-publishing public/projects/game-academy/ — it stays down until its sprites are converted to WebP in the sibling repo.
- Cache-Control / Render edge-caching changes.
- Any change to how egress is bucketed by slug — that shipped in be3c6b0 and validated clean.

## Engineering standards

Before writing any code, read `/home/bilko/.npm/_npx/5346543b21849140/node_modules/claude-code-session-manager/plugins/session-manager-dev/skills/develop/standards.md` — it has the Performance, Debugging,
API-reuse, TDD, and Execution-discipline rules that apply to this PRD. Every rule in it is
mandatory, especially Execution discipline (bounded commands, verify before done, the
finish-protocol sentinel).

Author: Bilko <StanislavBG@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Aug 13 15:40:34 2026 -0700

    fix(server): stop SPA-fallback 404 handler from double-sending and crashing the process
    
    Root cause: app.setNotFoundHandler (server/index.ts) is an async handler
    that called reply.send(...) without returning it. Fastify's wrapThenable
    resolves an async handler's own promise as soon as the function body
    finishes, but reply.sent only flips true once the raw HTTP response has
    actually finished writing (raw.writableEnded) — which happens after our
    async onSend hooks (CSP nonce injection in security-headers.ts, egress
    metering in egress.ts) resolve. That gap let Fastify believe nothing had
    been sent and call reply.send(undefined) a second time on top of the
    in-flight send, throwing an uncaught ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT that killed
    the process. This hit ANY unmatched path served by the SPA fallback in
    production (not just /projects/ paths) once redirect:true's static
    wildcard route fell through to callNotFound().
    
    Fix: return reply.send(...) from both branches so the handler's promise
    resolves via Reply's own thenable, which only resolves once the response
    truly ends — closing the race.
    
    Adds tests/spa-fallback-notfound-crash.test.ts, which boots the real
    built server as a child process and asserts /api/health still responds
    after hitting five unmatched/edge URL shapes (unknown slug + file,
    unknown slug bare, known slug + missing file, known slug trailing-slash
    redirect, unrelated top-level 404). Verified this test fails on all 5
    cases against the pre-fix build and passes after the fix.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

# Goal

Bilko is a host platform, so central usage monitoring should be a platform capability — readable by whoever operates the platform, not only by a human clicking through a browser session. Today the only way to read per-project egress is GET /api/admin/egress or /admin/observability, both gated on a Clerk JWT that exists only inside a signed-in browser. That makes the platform's own usage data unreachable to any agent, script, cron, or headless session — including the ones that maintain the platform. Add a usage report tool to the bilko-host MCP, which already holds a direct Turso client and is the established control plane for host operations.

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A new bilko-host MCP tool (suggested name `usage_report`) returns per-project egress: for each project slug, bytes out and request count over a caller-specified trailing window (default 7 days), sorted by bytes descending, including bytesPerRequest.
- [ ] The tool reads api_egress_daily through the existing Turso client in mcp-host-server/src/db.ts — it does NOT call the host's HTTP API and therefore does NOT require a Clerk JWT.
- [ ] Output distinguishes the static:<slug> buckets from the /api/* route rows, and explicitly surfaces static:_host and static:_other rather than hiding them, since _host currently absorbs top-level static dirs (/outdoor-hours/, /apps/, /session-manager-operations/) that belong to real projects.
- [ ] The tool reports the window it actually covered and the earliest date present in the table, so a caller can tell "no traffic" apart from "metering only started on <date>".
- [ ] Running the tool against the local dev DB with no rows returns a clean empty result with that explanation, not an error or a bare [].
- [ ] README/tool description states plainly that these are capacity-signal numbers measured at the origin, not Render billing figures, and that they will under-report by up to the flush interval on every process restart.
- [ ] mcp-host-server builds and its existing tools are unaffected.

# Implementation notes

The control plane already exists — this is one tool, not an architecture change.

- mcp-host-server/src/server.ts registers tools via server.registerTool(...); see `list_projects` at line ~175 and `publish_static_project` at ~313 for the established shape (zod inputSchema, ok()/err() helpers).
- mcp-host-server/src/db.ts:14-16 already builds a libsql client from TURSO_DATABASE_URL / TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN, falling back to the local data/contentgrade.db file. Reuse it. This is exactly why the MCP can read production without touching Clerk.
- The query shape to reuse is server/egress.ts topEgress() (lines 171-183) — SUM(requests), SUM(bytes) grouped by route over `date >= ?`, plus the bytesPerRequest derivation. Do not duplicate the SQL by hand if it can be shared; if sharing across the two packages is awkward, copy it with a comment pointing at the original.
- Slug convention: static rows are stored with route = `static:<slug>` (server/egress.ts:92,147). `static:_host` = host chrome and any top-level static dir; `static:_other` = unrecognised slug, cardinality-bounded.

KNOWN ACCURACY GAP worth surfacing in the tool output rather than silently inheriting: only /projects/<slug>/ paths bucket to a named slug. OutdoorHours serves its ~168 MB data tree from top-level /outdoor-hours/, so those bytes land in static:_host, not static:outdoor-hours. Same for /apps/ and /session-manager-operations/. A follow-up PRD should map known top-level static dirs to their owning slug; for now the tool should not present _host as if it were purely host chrome.

Depends on 996 (the crash-loop fix): while the service restarts every few minutes the in-process egress buffer is dropped on each restart, so any report built now reads low and would be misleading.

# Out of scope

- Adding a non-Clerk auth path to the host's HTTP API — the MCP's direct DB access is the right seam, and punching an API-key hole in requireAdmin is a security change nobody asked for.
- Reconciling these numbers against Render's billing figures.
- Fixing the top-level-static-dir attribution gap — note it in the output, fix it in a follow-up.

## Engineering standards

Before writing any code, read `/home/bilko/.npm/_npx/5346543b21849140/node_modules/claude-code-session-manager/plugins/session-manager-dev/skills/develop/standards.md` — it has the Performance, Debugging,
API-reuse, TDD, and Execution-discipline rules that apply to this PRD. Every rule in it is
mandatory, especially Execution discipline (bounded commands, verify before done, the

Author: Bilko <StanislavBG@gmail.com>

    feat(mcp-host): add usage_report tool for per-project egress
    
    Bilko's own usage/egress data was only reachable via a Clerk-gated
    HTTP endpoint (browser session required), so no agent, cron, or
    headless session could read it — including the ones that maintain
    the platform. usage_report reads api_egress_daily through the MCP's
    existing direct Turso client, splitting static:<slug> project buckets
    from raw /api/* route rows, surfacing static:_host/_other explicitly,
    and reporting the earliest date in the table so "no traffic" reads
    differently from "metering hasn't started yet".

  {
    title: 'Per-project egress/usage report',
    description:
      'Reads api_egress_daily directly through this MCP\'s own Turso client — no Clerk JWT, no browser, safe for cron/headless callers. Returns per-project static-asset egress (bytes out + request count, sorted by bytes descending, with bytesPerRequest) over a trailing window (default 7 days), plus the raw /api/* route rows reported separately (those are route *patterns*, not resolved to a project slug). ' +
      'IMPORTANT: these are capacity-signal numbers measured at the origin server, NOT Render billing figures — Render bills at the edge/CDN layer, which can differ. They also under-report by up to the in-process flush interval (60s) on every process restart, because the egress buffer is in-memory until flushed. ' +
      'static:_host and static:_other are surfaced explicitly rather than filtered out: _host currently absorbs top-level static dirs that belong to real projects but aren\'t served under /projects/<slug>/ (e.g. OutdoorHours\' large hourly-data tree at top-level /outdoor-hours/, plus /apps/ and /session-manager-operations/) — so _host is not purely host chrome today. _other is traffic to an unrecognised /projects/<x>/ slug. Also reports the earliest date present in the table so a caller can tell "no traffic in this window" apart from "metering only started on <date>".',
    inputSchema: {
      days: z.number().int().positive().default(7).describe('Trailing window size in days. Default 7.'),
    },
  },
  async ({ days }) => {
    try {
      const earliestRow = await mcpGet<{ earliest: string | null }>(
        `SELECT MIN(date) AS earliest FROM api_egress_daily`,
      );
      const earliestDate = earliestRow?.earliest ?? null;

      if (!earliestDate) {
        return ok(JSON.stringify({
          empty: true,
          explanation:
            'api_egress_daily has no rows in this database. Either this is a fresh/local dev DB that has never seen traffic, or the egress meter has not flushed yet (60s interval). This is not an error.',
          window: { requestedDays: days },
          static: [],
          api: [],
        }, null, 2));
      }

      const since = dayKey(Date.now() - days * 86_400_000);
      const through = dayKey(Date.now());

      const staticRows = await mcpAll<{ slug: string; requests: number; bytes: number }>(
        `SELECT SUBSTR(route, ${STATIC_ROUTE_PREFIX.length + 1}) AS slug,
                SUM(requests) AS requests, SUM(bytes) AS bytes
           FROM api_egress_daily
          WHERE date >= ? AND route LIKE 'static:%'
          GROUP BY slug
          ORDER BY bytes DESC`,
        [since],
      );

      const apiRows = await mcpAll<{ method: string; route: string; requests: number; bytes: number }>(
        `SELECT method, route, SUM(requests) AS requests, SUM(bytes) AS bytes
           FROM api_egress_daily
          WHERE date >= ? AND route NOT LIKE 'static:%'
          GROUP BY method, route
          ORDER BY bytes DESC`,
        [since],
      );

      const withRate = <T extends { requests: number; bytes: number }>(r: T) => ({
        ...r,
        bytesPerRequest: r.requests ? Math.round(r.bytes / r.requests) : 0,
      });

      const out = {
        empty: false,
        window: { requestedDays: days, sinceDate: since, throughDate: through },
        earliestDateInTable: earliestDate,
        static: staticRows.map(withRate),
        api: apiRows.map(withRate),
        notes: [
          'Capacity signal, not Render billing — measured at the origin, not the CDN edge.',
          'Under-reports by up to the flush interval (60s) on every process restart.',
          'static:_host absorbs some top-level static dirs that belong to real projects (e.g. outdoor-hours\' data tree, /apps/, /session-manager-operations/) — treat _host as inflated until that attribution gap is fixed in a follow-up.',
          '`api` rows are route PATTERNS (e.g. "/api/projects/:slug/feedback"), not resolved per-project — they are not folded into the per-slug `static` numbers.',
        ],
      };
      return ok(JSON.stringify(out, null, 2));
    } catch (e: unknown) {
      return err((e as Error).message);
    }
  },
);

**Yes, collecting now:**

|---|---|---|
| `/api/*` matched routes | **Per endpoint** — keyed on route *pattern* (`GET /api/projects/:slug/feedback`), with bytes + requests + bytesPerRequest | `2727290`, ~12:03 PM PDT |
| Static / project assets | **Per project slug** (`static:game-academy`), plus `static:_host` and `static:_other` | `be3c6b0`, deployed ~12:55 PM PDT |

So for API endpoints, yes — genuinely per-endpoint. For static traffic, **no** — it's per *project*, not per endpoint or per file. That was a deliberate cardinality choice (keying on resolved URLs would make the meter itself the problem), but it means you can see "game-academy is heavy" and not "these 10 sprites over 2 MB are why."

## Three blind spots I found reading the hooks

**1. Streamed API responses record 0 bytes.** `sizeOf()` (`egress.ts:69-75`) returns 0 for anything that isn't a string/Buffer/Uint8Array. At least two API routes send streams:
```
server/routes/manual.ts:167        return reply.send(createReadStream(full));
server/routes/project-events.ts:101  return sendFile.call(reply, `projects/${slug}/data-events.ndjson`);
```
The Field Manual download — a whole file — is currently booked as **free**. That's the same class of mistake the static meter was built to fix, still live on the API side.

**2. Unmatched `/api/*` 404s are counted nowhere.** The onSend hook requires a matched route (`egress.ts:133`); the onResponse hook early-returns on any `/api/` path (`egress.ts:145`). A 404 under `/api/` falls between them. Small bytes, but it means request volume from probing/scanning is invisible.

**3. No per-asset attribution**, as above.

A wrong zero is worse than a missing row — it reads as "this endpoint is free."

**Queued PRD 998** to close all three, including a bounded top-N heavy-hitter design for per-file attribution (top 50 paths/day, remainder folded into `_rest`) so you get file-level answers without unbounded keys.

# Goal

The egress meter now covers /api/* route patterns and per-project static buckets, but three categories of bytes are still counted as zero or not counted at all. Two of them are on routes that serve whole files, so they are exactly the shape most likely to be expensive. Close them so "we are collecting usage per endpoint" is true without asterisks.

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Streamed /api/* responses record real byte counts instead of 0. server/egress.ts:69-75 sizeOf() returns 0 for anything that is not a string/Buffer/Uint8Array, and at least two API routes send streams: server/routes/manual.ts:167 (reply.send(createReadStream(full))) and server/routes/project-events.ts:101 (reply.sendFile(...)). Verified by requesting each and asserting the recorded bytes are non-zero and match the file size.
- [ ] Unmatched /api/* requests (404s) are recorded somewhere rather than vanishing. Today the onSend hook requires a matched route pattern (server/egress.ts:133) and the onResponse hook early-returns on any /api/ path (server/egress.ts:145), so a 404 under /api/ is counted by neither. Bucket them under a single bounded key (e.g. `api:_notfound`) — never per-URL.
- [ ] Per-asset attribution is available for static traffic without unbounded cardinality: it must be possible to answer "which FILE under a project burned the bytes", not only "which project". Suggested approach: a bounded top-N heavy-hitter table (e.g. top 50 paths by bytes per day, everything else folded into an `_rest` row) rather than a row per URL. Whatever the design, state the cardinality bound explicitly in a comment.
- [ ] The existing per-project and per-route numbers are unchanged in shape and key naming — usage_report and /api/admin/egress keep working without modification to their callers.
- [ ] Tests cover all three: a streamed API route records non-zero bytes, an unmatched /api/ 404 lands in its bucket, and per-asset rows stay bounded when N distinct URLs are requested.
- [ ] pnpm test and pnpm build both pass.

# Implementation notes

Read server/egress.ts in full first — the design constraints in its header comment (never key on resolved URL, never write on the request path, never fail a response) still apply and are the reason the current gaps exist.

The likely unifying fix for gaps 1 and 2: the onResponse hook already reads Content-Length correctly (server/egress.ts:121-126, 140-153) and that mechanism works for streams. Consider routing ALL responses through the onResponse Content-Length path and keeping onSend only where a payload measurement is genuinely better, rather than maintaining two measurement strategies with different blind spots. If you do that, be careful not to double-count — there is an existing regression test for exactly that at tests/egress.test.ts:187 and :200.

Note Content-Length may be absent on chunked/streamed responses. If so, measure by counting bytes written to the raw socket rather than reintroducing a zero. Do not silently record 0 — a wrong zero is worse than a missing row because it reads as "this endpoint is free".

For gap 3, the motivating case is concrete: game-academy's 116.5 MB was 117 individual sprite PNGs, and identifying that required manual du + curl work. Per-project granularity would have said "game-academy is heavy" but not "these 10 files over 2 MB are the problem".

Do not regress the accuracy note already surfaced in usage_report's output about static:_host absorbing top-level dirs (/outdoor-hours/, /apps/, /session-manager-operations/) — that gap is tracked separately and should stay visible until fixed.

# Out of scope

- Fixing the top-level-static-dir attribution gap (static:_host inflation) — separate follow-up.
- Cache-Control headers or Render edge-caching configuration.
- Reconciling any of these numbers against Render billing.

Author: Bilko <StanislavBG@gmail.com>
Date:   Thu Aug 13 16:17:01 2026 -0700

    fix(egress): close streamed-response, unmatched-404, and per-file gaps in bandwidth meter
    
    Streamed /api/* responses (manual.ts's file download, project-events.ts's
    sendFile fallback) recorded 0 bytes because the old onSend hook only
    measured string/Buffer/Uint8Array payloads. Replaced it with an onRequest
    wrap of the raw response's write/end plus an onResponse hook that prefers
    Content-Length and falls back to actual bytes written to the socket, so a
    stream never books as free. Unmatched /api/* 404s now land in a single
    bounded api:_notfound bucket instead of vanishing between the two hooks.
    Added static_asset_daily for per-file (not just per-project) static egress,
    bounded to top-50-by-bytes + one folded _rest row per (date, slug) via
    pruneAssetOverflow on every flush, with concurrent flushes (timer + the
    admin endpoint's on-demand flush) serialized onto one in-flight promise so
    the prune's select-then-delete can't double-count.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
